title: Audit Console: faceted search, cursor pagination, and streamed JSON/CSV exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Enhance the Audit Log Console with robust faceted search, deterministic cursor-based pagination, and a streamed export pipeline that supports large CSV and newline-delimited JSON downloads without blocking the UI. This ticket covers API surface changes, backend export streaming, frontend UX for saved searches and export monitoring, and access controls aligned with RBAC v2 and SSO-scoped permissions.
acceptance_criteria: Console search supports multi-field faceted filtering (actor, action, resource, team, time window, outcome) and free-text query with boolean ops
Pagination operates via opaque cursor tokens for stable next/prev navigation and supports page sizes up to 200
Export endpoint streams results and produces both CSV and NDJSON; frontend triggers export and polls export status while download is available via signed URL
Saved searches can be persisted per-team and shared with role-based edit/view permissions (RBAC v2)
Exports respect data retention and redaction policies and are logged as audit events themselves
Automated tests cover query correctness, pagination invariants, export integrity for >5M rows using a representative dataset
tasks: API: add /audit/search endpoint with facet parameters and cursor response format
Backend: implement export streaming job using chunked responses and signed S3 URL generation
Indexing: ensure audit events are indexed with faceted fields and time buckets for efficient queries
Frontend: faceted filter UI, saved query UI, export progress modal, and download handling
RBAC: check permission checks for saved query visibility and export initiation
QA: synthetic load test to validate export memory and throughput behavior
Docs: update console help and API reference with examples and limits
tradeoffs: Cursor-based pagination avoids offset scans but makes deep random access harder; we accept this for predictable performance
Streaming exports will rely on eventual consistency of the OLAP index; export snapshotting would add complexity and cost
Implementing server-side CSV generation reduces frontend complexity but increases backend I/O; we will use streaming to limit memory footprint
tech_notes: Prefer ClickHouse or OpenSearch aggregations for facet counts depending on query pattern; prototype shows ClickHouse is ~2x faster for wide time ranges
Cursor token will encode timestamp + shard cursor + filter hash and be HMAC-signed to prevent tampering
Export job runs as ephemeral task with backpressure-friendly IO, writes to object store in compressed ndjson, and issues signed GET URL valid for 24 hours
Rate limit export initiation per org and require export permission scope; log export events to audit stream for compliance
